claim: C1: the direction of effect of SLC19A1 rs1051266 (RFC1 codon 27, His27/Arg27) on folate status is contested. Two independent groups report higher folate in His27 carriers (PMID:19650776, red-cell folate in Northern Irish women; PMID:10993718, plasma folate in the MTHFR 677CT stratum of 169 healthy subjects). One group reports that His27 lowers cellular folate uptake (PMID:15964598, higher extracellular-to-intracellular folate ratio; PMID:16750224, dietary folate tracked red-cell folate in GG and GA but not AA carriers). C2: because the direction is contested, methylation_panel.json scores no genotype at this locus (all Standard), keeps it as context, and records both sides.
not_claimed: That either direction is correct. That the locus has no effect on folate metabolism. Anything about methotrexate response or disease risk, which the row's other two citations (PMID:24597986, PMID:33935279) concern and which this change does not use as evidence for either direction.

claim_mapping.PMID:19650776: His27 carriers (GA, AA) had higher red-cell folate than GG among women (P=0.02); not associated in men or with serum folate or homocysteine. Supports the higher-folate side.
claim_mapping.PMID:10993718: 80AA/677CT individuals had higher plasma folate than 80GG/677CT (P=0.02). Supports the higher-folate side, within one MTHFR stratum.
claim_mapping.PMID:15964598: The 80A allele raised the extracellular-to-intracellular folate ratio, consistent with lower cellular uptake. Supports the lower-uptake side.
claim_mapping.PMID:16750224: Dietary folate correlated with red-cell folate in GG and GA but not AA carriers. Supports the lower-uptake side, as an absence of correlation rather than a measured reduction.
claim_mapping.PMID:24597986: Already cited. Meta-analysis finding no association with methotrexate toxicity in paediatric ALL. Context only; not used for either direction.
claim_mapping.PMID:33935279: Already cited. Meta-analysis of congenital heart disease risk. Context only; not used for either direction.

allele_frame: The literature's 80A/80G naming (G80A, c.80G>A) and the panel's A80G (c.80A>G on NM_194255.4) use the same base letter for the same residue: 80A is His27 and 80G is Arg27 (data/science-evidence/2026-08-10-slc19a1-rs1051266-nomenclature-2023/). So the papers' 80AA is the panel's AA, and 'His27 carriers' is the frame-independent name the panel prose uses.
high_stakes_two_source_rule: C1 is a claim that the evidence conflicts. It is met by opposite findings on folate status from independent groups. The higher-folate side has two independent groups: Chango et al. (INSERM U-308, France) and Stanisławska-Sachadyn et al. (Northern Ireland), with no shared authors. The lower-uptake side is ONE group: Yates Z appears on both PMID:15964598 and PMID:16750224, as does Lucock M(D), so those two count once. This is a wellness-panel, evidence-level-1 locus, not a clinical call, and the change only withholds a direction, so a single group on one side is enough to establish that the direction is not settled.
